title: Add .dockerignore for cam-worker image build context
description: docker build for the cam-worker image uses build context '.' (repo root) with no .dockerignore, so node_modules, dist, .git, .claude logs, claude-code-harness, and *.bun-build temps are all tarred and sent to the daemon each build. The Dockerfile never COPYs the context (installs via apt/npm; workspace is bind-mounted at run), so this is pure wasted transfer. Add a .dockerignore excluding node_modules, dist, .git, .claude, *.bun-build, coverage, and other non-build artifacts. Surfaced during CAM-175 (found a 4.9G context from ~84 orphan .bun-build files).

spec.scope: CAM-177 adds a .dockerignore at the repo root so the cam-worker (.devcontainer) image build stops tarring the entire repo to the daemon. The .devcontainer/Dockerfile performs exactly one COPY (.devcontainer/claude-config.json to /home/bun/.claude.json) and bind-mounts the workspace at run time, so every other file in the build context is wasted transfer; CAM-175 saw a 4.9G context from orphan .bun-build files. IN SCOPE: a repo-root .dockerignore using the allowlist idiom that ignores everything and re-includes only the one COPYed file: a header comment explaining the rule and its maintenance, then the four ordered lines star, then bang-dot-devcontainer, then dot-devcontainer-slash-star, then bang-dot-devcontainer-slash-claude-config.json; a golden-fixture test asserting the file content; and a behavioral proof that docker build -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile dot still succeeds with a drastically smaller transferred context (run by the reviewer or operator where docker is available, since macOS CI may lack docker). OUT OF SCOPE: a denylist enumeration of individual artifacts, templating the .dockerignore into downstream cam projects (the cam-worker image is cam-cli internal), and any change to the Dockerfile or the build command.
acceptanceCriteria: A .dockerignore exists at the repo root containing, in order, the four allowlist lines (star; then bang dot-devcontainer; then dot-devcontainer slash star; then bang dot-devcontainer slash claude-config.json), preceded by a header comment explaining the ignore-all-but-one rule and that a new Dockerfile COPY requires a matching allow line. A golden-fixture test asserts this content.

docker build -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile with the repo root as context still succeeds (the COPY of .devcontainer/claude-config.json resolves) and the transferred build context drops from gigabyte scale to kilobyte scale. This behavioral proof is run by the reviewer or operator where docker is available; macOS CI may lack docker.
gotchas: The re-include-a-nested-file-under-an-excluded-parent idiom requires BuildKit (last-match-wins evaluation); the legacy builder cannot re-include a file whose parent directory was excluded. cam container-mode uses modern docker, so BuildKit is the default.
The .devcontainer directory must be un-ignored before re-including the nested file; a bare star plus a single re-include of the nested file can fail on some builders, hence the four-line form.
The .dockerignore is brittle to a future Dockerfile COPY: adding a COPY requires adding a matching re-include line or the build breaks confusingly; the header comment must document this.
With -f .devcontainer/Dockerfile the Dockerfile is read directly and not from the build context, so excluding it via star is fine and does not break the build.
domainTerms: build context: the file tree sent to the docker daemon on build; the cam-worker image COPYs exactly one file, so the context should be reduced to that single file via an allowlist .dockerignore.
